IMPORTANT POINTS

# Page 7^page=7
1. NPS Swasthya Scheme is designed to allow pension contributions to be linked with healthcare expenses. 2. Eligibility: All Indian citizens are eligible to join the scheme voluntarily, provided they have a Common Scheme Account alongside the NPS Swasthya Pension Scheme Account. 3. Age Limit: Subscribers above the age of 40 can transfer their contributions to this healthcare scheme from the NPS Common Scheme Account. 4. Contributions: Subscribers can transfer up to 30% of their own and employer’s contributions to the healthcare corpus. 5. Withdrawals: Up to 25% of the subscriber’s own contributions can be withdrawn at a time for medical purposes. 6. No Limit on Withdrawals: There is no restriction on the number of medical withdrawals allowed. 7. No Waiting Period: No waiting period for withdrawals, as long as the minimum corpus of ₹50,000 has been accumulated before the first withdrawal. 8. Premature Exit for Critical Treatment: If the cost of treatment exceeds 70% of the total corpus, a subscriber can opt for a 100% lump-sum premature exit. 9. Direct Settlement: Any withdrawn or exited amounts are paid directly to hospitals or insurance providers for claims. 10. Surplus Credit: Any surplus after claims are settled is credited back to the Common Scheme Account.

# Page 8^page=8
11. Medical Expense Focus: The scheme is focused on medical expense financing rather than income replacement during retirement. 12. Healthcare-linked Pension: The scheme operates as a healthcare-linked pension innovation within a Regulatory Sandbox under the government. 13. Separate Healthcare Corpus: The healthcare corpus is kept separate from the subscriber’s retirement savings. 14. Individual Risk: The scheme operates under the principle that healthcare expenses are borne by the individual, not pooled like insurance. 15. Transparency: Clear disclosures are mandatory about fees, claims process, exit options, and grievance redressal. 16. Pension Fund Responsibility: The Pension Fund is responsible for resolving any grievances related to the scheme. 17. Explicit Consent: Subscribers must provide explicit digital consent, adhering to the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. 18. Regulatory Framework: It is introduced as a central sector scheme under a Regulatory Sandbox as a proof of concept.

# Page 9^page=9
19. Financial Allocation: The scheme operates on a contributory basis, with no fixed budget, and is funded by the subscriber. 20. Limited Duration: The scheme is available only during the Regulatory Sandbox period, which is a limited- duration proof of concept for future implementation.
